acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. WHAT 'VERIFIED ORIGINAL SENDER THROUGH THE FORWARDING ARRANGEMENT' CAN AND CANNOT MEAN BEFORE IB-s-6 HAS INSPECTED A REAL MAILBOX. This cell's fixtures assume the SHARED AnalysisRequest.sender_evidence contract shape verbatim (IB-s-18): verified (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED/REJECTED), original_sender_address, verification_method (FORWARDING_ARRANGEMENT_HEADERS/ORIGINAL_MIME/UNKNOWN), display_from_used (bool). WHAT THIS CAN MEAN TODAY: a FIELD-LEVEL contract that four downstream cells (this one, B6, B7, B9 via AnalysisRequest) all validate against, so a change to the evidence shape breaks visibly rather than silently. WHAT IT CANNOT MEAN YET: the METHOD BY WHICH those four fields are actually populated. Row IRPT_BCKEND-S3 (filed at IB-s-18's cut) already records that the brief names NO existing Graph/certificate mailbox implementation and that infra/aws/ec2/opal-gateway/app/config.py is an UNVERIFIED candidate. Until B6 inspects that gateway (or whatever mailbox client actually exists) and states EXACTLY which Graph API fields it reads -- Internet Message Headers 'Authentication-Results', a DKIM/SPF verdict, the raw MIME From vs a forwarding X-header -- this cell's verified='VERIFIED' fixtures are a HYPOTHESIS about what B6 will produce, not a measurement of it. Concretely: 'FORWARDING_ARRANGEMENT_HEADERS' as a verification_method NAMES a mechanism (headers set by a trusted forwarding arrangement) that this cell has never seen a real header for. If the real mailbox implementation turns out to verify via SPF/DKIM alignment instead of a forwarding header, the enum value ORIGINAL_MIME might be the truer label, or a third value may be needed -- and gate.py's _VALID_METHODS tuple would need a matching edit, which is exactly the kind of drift a single shared contract is supposed to prevent but cannot prevent for a field whose REAL values are still unmeasured. This cell's SPOOFING check (display_from_used != False) is the one arm I am confident survives contact with the real mailbox regardless of method, because the shared contract's const:false is a STATEMENT ABOUT THE FIELD'S MEANING, not about how it is measured.

2. IS THE OWNER NAMED HERE THE RIGHT MAINTAINER? '0.7.0_AE_CloudOps' is the decomposition's OWN assignment (s.2), not my choice, and I did not second-guess it -- but I can name what the choice implies and what it does not settle. AE_CloudOps is the estate's cloud-infrastructure seat; the policy IS infrastructure (Terraform, IAM, S3 layout) so the assignment is coherent on THAT axis. What it does NOT settle: the policy also encodes a BUSINESS decision (which domains map to which firms, and the special-casing of the Opal domain), and a firm's own domain change (a rebrand, a new sending domain) is a data/firm_registry.json edit that AE_CloudOps does not own end to end -- data/firm_registry.json's own _meta names NFRA_PSTMRT / an Andrew-direct handover as its authority, a DIFFERENT owner than 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps. So today: the registry's OWNER and the policy DOCUMENT's owner are two different seats, joined only by test_policy_completeness.py's assertion that their firm SETS agree -- the test cannot verify that the RIGHT PERSON was consulted when a firm's domain (as opposed to its presence) changes, only that the firm ID sets stay in sync. A firm whose email_domain is edited in place (not added or removed) passes completeness silently while re-routing every future message from that firm's old domain to Quarantined -- worth a second owner's eyes specifically on domain EDITS, not just adds.

3. WHAT AN OPERATOR STILL CANNOT SEE FROM firm_destination_policy.json ALONE. (i) WHETHER THE IAM CONDITIONS ACTUALLY ENFORCE WHAT THE POLICY DECLARES. The JSON names an execution_role per firm; nothing in the file states that role's policy is SCOPED to that firm's prefix -- that fact lives in iam_firm_conditions.tf and was verified separately (get-role read the TRUST policy only; the ATTACHED permission policy's content was verified by 0-diff terraform plan, a DIFFERENT instrument, not by reading this JSON). A reader trusting the JSON alone would be trusting a claim the JSON cannot itself prove. (ii) WHETHER A GIVEN ROLE HAS EVER BEEN ASSUMED. No Lambda exists yet; the roles are live but unused, and row IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S6 records that comp-iam's own census cannot see this either. (iii) THE EXPORT-DESTINATION GAP IB-s-17's S17-AC3 ALREADY NAMED, WHICH THIS POLICY DOES NOT CLOSE. This policy's destinations mirror layout.json's three families exactly (intake, requests, generations, plus the three generation artifacts); it inherits IB-s-17's finding that a PERFORMANCE export -- one with no YCharts generation attempt to nest under -- has no declared prefix and therefore no enumerated destination or IAM condition here either. IB-s-14 will hit this gap directly. (iv) WHETHER QUARANTINE IS EVER DRAINED. The policy names quarantine's prefix and role; nothing anywhere (this cell, IB-s-17, or the decomposition as read so far) names a process that reviews or ages out a quarantined item -- it is a write-only destination with no declared reader. (v) THAT policy_version '1' HAS NEVER CHANGED. A single version string with no history gives an operator no way to tell 'this is the first version' from 'this has been silently regenerated many times with no version bump' -- the local_file resource has no logic that increments it, so a future edit to roles.tf would apply under the SAME version number unless a human remembers to bump it by hand.

mutant.description: The load-bearing claims are that a firm's destination is only ever its own, that a cross-firm/spoofed/contradictory/unknown origin never binds, and that a bound firm cannot be reassigned. FOUR red-first mutants, TWO of which found real gaps in the FIRST draft of the battery/tests rather than in gate.py itself, and BOTH are fixed and reported here rather than quietly patched. (1) Disabling destination_for's cross-firm check (arm b) fired cleanly first try. (2) Disabling the spoofing signal (arm c) CRASHED the battery with an AttributeError -- a spoofed fixture that wrongly bound has no .reason attribute, and the printer assumed every outcome carried one. Fixed to report the wrong bind as data instead of crashing on it. (3) Disabling BoundRequest.__setattr__'s raise (arm d) did NOT fire against the criterion's own three named attempts (set/rebind/delete on .firm_id) -- because .firm_id is a read-only PROPERTY with no setter, so Python's own descriptor protocol independently blocks all three regardless of __setattr__. This is a WEAK mutant that exposed a real design fact (immutability here is TWO-LAYERED, not one) rather than a real gap; the test suite and battery were both strengthened with a FOURTH attempt against `_binding`, an actual __slots__ member the property does not protect, which DOES discriminate the mutation. (4) Pointing the battery's arm (f) at a nonexistent role name fired cleanly.
mutant.expected: Each mutant must produce rc=1, WITHHOLD the token, print an arm-tagged ERROR line, and restore byte-for-byte. A mutant that instead crashes uncontrolled, or that a criterion's own literal wording lets survive via an UNRELATED mechanism, is named as such rather than counted as a pass.
mutant.observed: 4 of 4 FIRED-AS-EXPECTED after both fixes. (b) cross-firm refusal disabled -> rc=1, 'a cross-firm destination request did NOT raise'. (c) spoofing signal disabled -> rc=1, 'spoofed display-From: never_firm=False right_type=False detail=BOUND to firm_id=\'49financial\' -- THIS FIXTURE SHOULD NEVER HAVE BOUND'. (d) __setattr__ disabled -> rc=1, 'only 3 of 4 mutation attempts raised' (the internal-slot attempt succeeding under the mutation, the property-guarded ones still blocked independently -- exactly the asymmetry the fourth attempt was added to surface). (f) nonexistent role -> rc=1, 'irpt-core-firm-nonexistent: rc=255 assumes_lambda=False'. All four files restored byte-for-byte (sha256 compared, 4 of 4 equal), battery green at rc=0 with the token before and after. 20 of 20 gate tests and the completeness suite were re-run clean after both battery fixes and the new test was added.
